tara: quick Q — with the year-end shutdown coming up, how does PTO accrual work for someone who starts Dec 20? can they use any carryover or do we prorate?

jess (People Ops): short answer: prorated for the month they start, yes. long answer: new hires earn accruals based on days active that month; Dec 20–31 would get the prorated fraction of the monthly accrual. carryover rules still apply to the employee's annual balance. :calendar:

mike: and carryover cap this year is still 40 hours, right? or did that change?

jess (People Ops): correct — standard carryover cap = 40 hours (unless you have an approved exception). any hours above 40 are auto-forfeited unless an exception is granted by people ops before Jan 31. exceptions are rare and require manager + people-ops approval (medical or compulsion reasons).

sarah: are there blackout dates for time-off requests during the shutdown? some teams need coverage.

jess (People Ops): yes — our company-wide holiday shutdown is Dec 24–Jan 1 (inclusive). for teams classified as "essential coverage" managers must submit a coverage rotation plan by Dec 10. managers should mark essential roles in the PTO portal. non-essential folks should book PTO via the normal flow.

tara: @jess any special process for approving carryover for folks who are on LOA during the cutoff?

jess (People Ops): LOA folks: accruals stop during unpaid LOA; if LOA overlaps cutoff we evaluate on a case-by-case basis. please DM the case to people-ops with LOA dates, manager note, and any supporting docs. deadline to request these exceptions is Jan 31.

alex: to confirm, if someone starts Dec 20 and gets prorated accrual for Dec, can they take that PTO during the shutdown or do they need manager sign-off?

jess (People Ops): they can take it, but manager approval required as usual. managers should prioritize fairness with coverage. if unsure, use the quick template shown below when submitting to the portal: 

```
Subject: Year-end PTO request (Prorated hire)
Employee: <name>
Start date: 2025-12-20
Requested dates: 2025-12-24 — 2026-01-01
PTO balance (as of request): <auto-filled>
Manager note: coverage plan attached / coverage by <peer name>
```

jess (People Ops): also — if a manager needs to approve >3 people off concurrently in a small team, please coordinate with adjacent teams for temporary coverage or use the "temporary coverage" Slack channel and tag ops.

people-ops-bot: Automated reminder: "Submit coverage rotation plans by Dec 10 to avoid approval delays." :robot_face: <https://hr.redwood.com/coverage-plans>

mike: is there a policy doc link for accrual math? would be useful to share with new hires.

jess (People Ops): sure — here's the quick doc: https://hr.redwood.com/pto-policy (has formulas for monthly prorate and carryover rules). i'll drop a short FAQ and a sample calc sheet in #announcements by EOD.

sarah: thanks! i'll remind my managers to put in their coverage plans.

tara: one last thing — do managers need to pre-approve carryover requests before Jan 31 or can people submit and then managers approve?

jess (People Ops): submit first in the portal, manager approval comes after submission. people-ops will not finalize exceptions without the manager's sign-off. process: submit -> manager approve -> people-ops review -> final decision.

alex: :thumbsup: got it.

people-ops-bot: Policy snippet: "Carryover exceptions: submit by Jan 31. Max auto-carryover 40h. Exceptions require manager + people-ops approval."

jess (People Ops): okay everyone — i'll post the FAQ + sample calc. ping me if you want me to review a specific exception before formal submission. :pray:
